layout_details.content: ## 7.5 Formula keys
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Keys to a formula (following the pattern "where X = Y") are coded as <def-list> with @list-content="formula", with the word "where" as the <label>. The elements of that list are coded as pairs inside <def-item>. Each <def-item> contains one <term> and one <def>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: $ L=\frac{\mu l}{2\pi}\left[\ln \left(\frac{4 l}{d}\right)-1\right] $ H where $ \mu $ $ =4\pi\times10^{-7} $ H/m; $ l $ is the length of the wire in m; $ d $ is the diameter of the wire in m.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## is coded as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html μ

= 4π × 10−7 H/m;

 l

is the length of the wire in m;

 ```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## IEC
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Legacy tagging at IEC sometimes uses <def-head> instead of <label> to code the word "where".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: <def-list> only allows the coding of pairs of <term> and <def>. If there is more than one definition for each <term> (e.g. a definition text and a symbol), a regular table will be used to code the key.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## ISO
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Under investigation for future implementation:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ISO aims to align with the Guidelines and use the above.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Until this is integrated into the ISO/CS production chain, formula keys will be coded in <array>. Example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

where

P is the bacterial concentration (cfu/ml);
Z is the average number of colonies in the three Petri dishes (cfu);
DF is the dilution factor.
```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 7.6 MathML
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The mathematical expression within the <disp-formula> or <inline-formula> is coded using <mml:math>. Its visual representation should be preserved as closely as possible, including spacing.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Every <mml:math> , irrespective of whether it is contained in a <disp-formula> or an <inlineformula> element, contains an @id number which may be different from the label of the <dispformula>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: If one <disp-formula> contains more than one mathematical expression laid out on separate lines, these are contained in one <mml:math>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The @id is prefixed "mml_m[number]", with [number] representing the sequential position of the <mml:math> element in the document, for example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<disp-formula id="formula_1">

  <label>(1)</label>

  <mml:math id="mml_m5">

    ...

  </mml:math>

</disp-formula>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The ID corresponds to the name of a graphical representation of the formula (.png) that is delivered inside the asset folder and can be used as an alternative in case of problems with the rendering of MathML.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: No detailed instructions are provided here for the coding of MathML; we assume that this will be handled by a specialized WYSIWYG tool that will generate the codes automatically.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 8 Figures
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 8.1 Elements and attributes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Editorial note A figure is made up of at least an image and a designation "Figure # - Title of Figure", e.g: Figure 1 - Rigid steel plate.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The figure is coded in <fig>.
layout_details.label: text

```html
<graphic xlink:href="asset/fig-1"/></fig>

```

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - figure notes are coded in <non-normative-note>
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - paragraphs between the graphic and the figure designation are coded in
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text
text

layout_details.content: ## 8.2 Sub-figures and multiple graphics within a figure
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
ISO The caption of a sub-figure (e.g. "a) - title of sub-figure") is coded in <title> within a <caption> within the <graphic>.

The rest of the sub-figure caption should be captured as a label within the <graphic> (excluding any trailing dash), for example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
<graphic xlink:href="fig_1.1" id="fig_1.1">

  <label>a)</label>

  <caption><title>title of sub-figure</title></caption>

</graphic>

IEC

If the figure contains multiple graphics, then each graphic is captured as a separate <graphic> within <fig>.

If the figure consists of multiple sub-figures (each with their own caption), then each subfigure is captured as a separate <fig> inside <figure-group>.

Each sub-figure has an @id based on its label.

For example:

<fig-group id="fig-3">

  <label>Figure 3</label>

  <caption>

    <title>Example for a typical cable arrangement for measurements of radiated disturbances in 3 m separation distance, Table-top EUT</title></caption>

    <fig id="fig-3a">

      <label>Figure 3a</label>

      <caption>

        <title>Top view</title></caption>

        <graphic xlink:href="asset/fig-3a"/></fig>

        <fig id="fig-3b">

          <label>Figure 3b</label>

          <caption>

            <title>Side view</title></caption>

            <graphic xlink:href="asset/fig-3b"/></fig></fig-group>

layout_details.content: ## 9 Terms and definitions
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.1 Subclauses inside a "Terms and Definitions" clause
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The terms and definitions clause can be subdivided: either to organize and group similar concepts, or to separate a terms and definitions subclause from another subclause, such as abbreviated terms.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## sound pressure
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: fluctuating pressure superimposed on the static pressure
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 1 to entry: Sound pressure is expressed in pascal.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Note 2 to entry: Sound pressure is usually expressed through the use of a decibel scale, as sound pressure level (see 3.1.4).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: is coded as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<term-sec id="con-3.1.3">

<label>3.1.3</label>

<txx:termEntry id="te-3.1.3">

<txx:langSet xml:lang="en">

<txx:definition>fluctuating pressure superimposed on the static pressure</txx:definition>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<txb:note id="nte-3.1.3-1">Sound pressure is expressed in pascal.</txb:note>

<txb:note id="nte-3.1.3-2">Sound pressure is usually expressed through the use of a decibel scale, as sound pressure level (see <xref ref-type="other" rid="con-3.1.4">3.1.4</xref>).</txb:note>

<txb:tig>

<txb:term id="ter-sound_pressurep">sound pressure</txb:term>

<txb:partOfSpeech value="noun"/>

<txb:normativeAuthorization value="preferredTerm"/>

<txb:termType value="fullForm"/></txb:tig>

<txb:tig>

<txb:term id="ter-p"><italic>p</italic></txb:term>

<txb:partOfSpeech value="noun"/>

<txb:normativeAuthorization value="admittedTerm"/>

<txb:termType value="symbol"/></txb:tig>

</txb:langSet></txb:termEntry></term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.2 Usage of TBX vs. <term-display>
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.2.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: There are two different options for tagging terms and definitions. Both structures occur optionally inside a the <term-sec> container element:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - one is TBX
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - the other is a simpler, less powerful alternative, <term-display>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
ISO ISO uses TBX exclusively.
IEC IEC uses TBX wherever possible. In redline documents and certain series where the elements are arranged in a special way and layout is important to the entry, IEC also uses , as described in 9.4.
layout_details.label: table

layout_details.content: The <term-sec> container element also includes <label>, which contains the number of the terminological entry.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.2.2 TBX (based exclusively on semantic information)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: TBX is a concept-oriented exchange format for data from terminological databases. The TBX element <tbx:termEntry> models a term using the TBX-namespace vocabulary and ontology for terms. It can record information about any number of synonymous terms and multiple languages. The TBX vocabulary in NISO STS is derived and extended from ISO 30042. For usage information and contents, see the documentation at: https://www.iso.org/schema/nisosts/v0.2/doc/tbx/index.html
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.2.3 <term-display> (more appearance oriented)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The NISO STS element <term-display> uses natural language to describe terms, and may incorporate semantic term elements such as definition ( <def> ) and part of speech ( <part-of-speech> ). Semantic tagging is encouraged, but not enforced. It is a more appearance-oriented encoding of terminological data that may be used when:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - a standards organization chooses not to employ TBX
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - it is difficult to generate the desired formatted display from a TBX entry
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - converting back-catalogue documents, in cases where it is difficult to create a useful TBX term entry from an appearance-oriented input document
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Generally, ISO and IEC will use TBX. In some cases of legacy conversion, however, IEC uses <termdisplay> to ensure all elements are correctly displayed. For usage, see 9.4 below.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.3 Terminological entries in TBX
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.3.1 Terms and definitions
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A terminological entry (<tbx:termEntry>) contains these core components (inside <tbx:langSet>):
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - Terms and their description (each term coded inside its own <tbx:tig>) - see 9.3.3
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - Definition (<tbx:definition>) - see 9.3.2
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For further information about these and other elements of TBX, see https://www.iso.org/schema/nisosts/v0.2/doc/tbx/index.html.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The ID of the terminological entry is derived from the entry number contained in <label> and is used for both <term-sec> and <tbx:termEntry>. IEC has an @id on <tbx:term> as well.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```xml

<term-sec id="sec_3.1">

    <label>3.1</label>

    <tbx:termEntry id="term_3.1">

        <tbx:langSet xml:lang="en">

            <tbx:definition>The point in an encoding...boundary.</tbx:definition>

            <tbx:tig>

                <tbx:term>alignment point</tbx:term>

                <tbx:partOfSpeech value="noun"/>

            </tbx:tig>

        </tbx:langSet>

    </tbx:termEntry>

</term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## IEC
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: <term-sec>: @id has prefix "con-”
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: <tbx:term-entry>: @id has prefix "te-"
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: <tbx:term>: @id corresponds to the term itself
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<term-sec id="con-3.1.3">

<label>3.1.3</label>

<txb:termEntry id="te-3.1.3">

<txb:langSet xml:lang="en">

<txb:definition>fluctuating pressure superimposed on the static pressure</txb:definition>

<txb:note id="nte-3.1.3-1">Sound pressure is expressed in pascal.</txb:note>

<txb:note id="nte-3.1.3-2">Sound pressure is usually expressed through the use of a decibel scale, as sound pressure level (see <xref ref-type="other" rid="con-

3.1.4">3.1.4</xref>).</txb:note>

<txb:tig>

<txb:term id="ter-sound_pressurep">sound pressure</txb:term>

<txb:partOfSpeech value="noun"/>

<txb:normativeAuthorization value="preferredTerm"/>

<txb:termType value="fullForm"/></txb:tig>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<tbx:tig>

<tbx:term id="ter-p"><italic>p</italic></tbx:term>

<tbx:partOfSpeech value="noun"/>

<tbx:normativeAuthorization value="admittedTerm"/>

<tbx:termType value="symbol"/></tbx:tig>

</tbx:langSet></tbx:termEntry></term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.3.2 Definitions
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A definition is coded in <tbx:definition>, inside <tbx:langSet>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A <break/> can be used to insert a line break in a definition if necessary.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.3.3 Terms and additional information on them
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Each term and its descriptive elements are contained in one individual <tbx:tig> (term information group). Terms are coded inside <tbx:term>, which is mandatory.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The elements used at ISO and IEC to describe terms are currently:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - <tbx:partOfSpeech> (mandatory)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - <tbx:normativeAuthorization>
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - <tbx:termType>
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - <tbx:grammaticalNumber>
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: <tbx:geographicalUsage> and <tbx:grammaticalGender> will probably be used in the future.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: "Part of speech" of a term
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: <tbx:partOfSpeech> is mandatory.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Possible values:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: noun
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - verb
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - adj
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - adv
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In NISO STS v.1.0, there is no value "undefined". Therefore, all legacy conversion uses "noun" as the default value. While this may be correct in most cases, it is not a reliable value. We therefore recommend not basing any programming on this value for now.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: electro-pneumatic continuous pressure control valve control valve which continuously modulates the pneumatic power of a system in response to a continuous electrical input signal and which links the electrical input quantity to a pressure value
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: is coded as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```xml

<term-sec id="sec_3.1">

    <label>3.1</label>

    <tbx:termEntry id="term_3.1">

        <tbx:langSet xml_lang="en">

            <tbx:definition>control valve which continuously modulates the pneumatic power

of a system in response of a continuous electrical input signal and which links the

electrical input quantity to a pressure value</tbx:definition>

            <tbx:tig>

                <tbx:term>electro-pneumatic continuous pressure control valve</tbx:term>

                <tbx:partOfSpeech value="noun"/>

            </tbx:tig>

        </tbx:langSet>

    </tbx:termEntry>

</term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Form of the term (<tbx:termType>)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: <tbx:termType> is optional but is generally used at ISO and IEC. If it is used, it can have these values in the ISO/IEC context:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: acronym
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
- acronym

- abbreviation

- fullForm (default value, can be omitted)

- symbol

- formula

- equation
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: 3. 13 data monitoring committee DMC independent committee that may be established by the sponsor to assess, at intervals, the progress of the clinical investigation, the safety data or the critical performance endpoints and to recommend the sponsor whether to continue, suspend, modify, or stop the clinical investigation
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: is coded as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```xml

<term-sec id="sec_3.13">

    <label>3.13</label>

    <tbx:termEntry id="term_3.13">

        <tbx:langSet xml:lang="en">

            <tbx:definition>independent committee that may be...

investigation</tbx:definition>

            <tbx:tig>

                <tbx:term>data monitoring committee</tbx:term>

                <tbx:partOfSpeech value="noun"/>

            </tbx:tig>

            <tbx:tig>

                <tbx:term>DMC</tbx:term>

                <tbx:partOfSpeech value="noun"/>

                <tbx:termType value="abbreviation"/>

            </tbx:tig>

            </tbx:langSet>

        </tbx:termEntry>

    </term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Term status (<tbx:normativeAuthorization>)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: <tbx:normativeAuthorization> is an optional element indicating the status of a term. It is generally used at ISO/IEC and can have these values:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - preferred (recommended)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - admitted (allowed)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - deprecated (for deprecated or obsolete terms, superseded terms, archaic terms, scientific-technical slang, terms indicated as "deprecated in this sense" [IEV] and other terms which are detrimental to domain communication)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<term-sec id="con-3.9">

<label>3.9</label>

<tbx:termEntry>

<tbx:langSet xml:lang="en">

<tbx:definition>radiant power incident on an element of a surface divided by the area of that

element</tbx:definition>

<tbx:source>

<std std-id="urn:iec:std:iec:60050-731:1991-12::::#con-731-1-25">

<std-ref>IEC 60050‑731:1991, 731‑1‑25</std-ref></std></tbx:source>

<tbx:tig>

<tbx:term id="ter-irradiance">irradiance</tbx:term>

<tbx:normativeAuthorization value="preferredTerm"/>

<tbx:termType value="fullForm"/></tbx:tig>

<tbx:tig>

<tbx:term id="ter-intensity">intensity</tbx:term>

<tbx:normativeAuthorization value="deprecatedTerm"/>

<tbx:termType value="fullForm"/></tbx:tig></tbx:langSet></tbx:termEntry></term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## and:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<term-sec id="con-3.1">

<label>3.1</label>

<txb:termEntry>

<txb:langSet xml:lang="en">

<txb:definition>fluctuating pressure superimposed on the static (barometric) pressure by the presence of sound</txb:definition>

<txb:note id="nte-3.1-1">It is expressed in pascal, Pa.</txb:note>

<txb:tig>

<txb:term id="ter-sound_pressure">sound pressure</txb:term>

<txb:normativeAuthorization value="preferredTerm"/>

<txb:termType value="fullForm"/></txb:tig>

<txb:tig>

<txb:term id="ter-p"><italic>p</italic></txb:term>

<txb:normativeAuthorization value="admittedTerm"/>

<txb:termType value="symbol"/></txb:tig></txb:langSet></txb:termEntry></term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.3.4 Examples in terminology
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: When coding with TBX, the "Example" keyword is removed from the content (use <tbx:example>).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
3.1 boundaries physical or site limits and/or organizational limits as defined by the organization

EXAMPLE A process: a group of processes: a site: an entire organization: multiple sites under the control of an organization.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: is coded as:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```xml

<term-sec id="sec_3.1">

    <label>3.1</label>

    <tbx:termEntry id="term_3.1">

        <tbx:langSet xml:lang="en">

            <tbx:definition>physical or site limits... organization</tbx:definition>

            <tbx:example>A process; a group... organization </tbx:example>

        ..

    </term-sec>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 9.3.5 Notes in terminology
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Terminological notes ("Note X to entry") are coded as <tbx:note>. When coding with TBX, the label "NOTE" or "Note X to entry" (or any other label) is removed from the content.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
3.4 audit findings results of the evaluation of the collected audit evidence (3.3) against audit criteria (3.2)

NOTE 1 Audit findings indicate conformity or nonconformity.

layout_details.content: ## 9.3.7 References to the other sections of the document [within TBX coding]
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The NISO metadata model allows for multiple instances of <std-meta>. This can be used for National metadata.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: # Annex B Coding Tables in NISO STS
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Tables are coded using the XHTML 1.1 table model. OASIS modules for the OASIS XML Exchange table model (based on the CALS table model) have been included in NISO STS, therefore <oasis:table> may be used in addition to or in place of the XHTML <table> element.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: However, this document will only describe tables using the XHTML 1.1 table model.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: There are very few differences between JATS and NISO coding of tables; one notable difference is that <caption> is now a child of <table-wrap> and not of <table>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.2 Text alignment of tables
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## B.2.1 Default vertical alignment of a table text
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - Use the value "top" as the default value for @valign.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - This should be applied for the element <col> which will automatically define the text alignment of the complete column.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - Whenever the defined alignment changes visually within the table/column, the applicable alignment should be coded with @valign separately for that cell(s)
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Table columns which have the alignment as visualized in the below images will be coded with @valign="top". Only the red highlighted cells in Table G.37 will be considered as different.

layout_details.content: ## B.2.2 Default horizontal alignment of a table text
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In XHTML, the default alignment of a table cell data is defined as "left".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Use @align="left" whenever the table cell data is aligned left as well as when it is not clear visually whether the cell data is left aligned or centered.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: When in doubt, this default value should be used.
